business_problem: Travelpass was spending too much time debugging a crash-prone, high-maintenance Databricks environment that made data delivery expensive, unreliable, and too difficult for a broader set of engineers and analysts to contribute to.
solution_summary: Travelpass moved from Databricks to Snowflake to replace a crash-prone, labor-intensive platform with a data foundation that its broader engineering team could actually use. Over six weeks, and with Snowflake Professional Services, the company migrated 30 TB of data and 134 pipelines and processes without business disruption. In Snowflake, hotel inventory, pricing, ad data, restaurant recommendations, sightseeing reservations, and other travel content can be transformed closer to the data, with clear spend visibility instead of opaque platform costs. Dynamic Tables let backend engineers, analysts, and other SQL-capable workers create pipelines declaratively, so data delivery to business units became 350% more efficient and the team reached more than 130 production Dynamic Tables within a week of migration. That freed Travelpass to spend less time debugging platform behavior and more time building curated traveler experiences on a governed, lower-cost data platform.

solution_components.name: Dynamic Tables
